what: Corcept Therapeutics develops medicines that block cortisol, the body's main stress hormone. Its approved product, Korlym, treats Cushing's syndrome, a condition of excess cortisol. Its newer compound relacorilant is designed to do the same with fewer side effects, and is also being studied in ovarian cancer.
customers: Endocrinologists treating Cushing's syndrome, and, if the oncology programmes succeed, oncologists treating ovarian and other cancers.
money: Oral medicine for hypercortisolism associated with Cushing's syndrome, sold in the United States.
moat: Cushing's syndrome is rare, so the prescriber base is small and Corcept has spent years building relationships with the specialists who treat it. Its cortisol-modulation chemistry is protected by a wide patent portfolio, which it has defended vigorously against generic challengers.
risks: The entire business currently rests on one product in one rare disease.
Korlym faces ongoing generic litigation. A loss would remove most of the revenue base before relacorilant is fully established.
The shares trade at about 51 times earnings and 60 times EV/EBITDA, prices that assume relacorilant succeeds commercially.
The oncology programme is the larger part of the upside and carries the usual risk that late-stage cancer trials disappoint.
Only five analysts cover the stock, so the $142.60 average target rests on very few views.
opportunities: Revenue has grown every year shown, from $366.0M in 2021 to $761.4M in 2025, with trailing revenue of about $963.6M.
The company is genuinely profitable, with about $159.4M of net income and $194.6M of free cash flow, which is unusual for a company of this type.
The balance sheet has $372.2M of cash against almost no debt, at $6.1M.
Cushing's syndrome is thought to be substantially under-diagnosed, and hypercortisolism in difficult-to-control diabetes is a much larger potential population.
watch: Relacorilant's transition from Korlym. Corcept's long-term value depends on moving patients to the newer, patent-protected medicine before generic competition reaches the old one.
